questions: Which elements should be removed when there are duplicates - all occurrences or just the extra ones?
If removing all duplicates, should we keep the first occurrence, last occurrence, or none at all?
What is the exact definition of "some elements" that occur more than once - does this mean we can choose which duplicates to remove?
Should the function handle empty lists, and if so, what should be returned?
Are there any constraints on the range of integers in the input list?
Should the function handle None input or non-list inputs, and if so, how?
What is the expected behavior when the input contains only one element?
Is the input list guaranteed to be non-None, or do we need to handle None as a possible input?
answers: All elements that occur more than once should be removed entirely (not just the extra occurrences) -- the result keeps only elements that appear exactly once in the original list.
